recreation_prompt_markdown:
Create a polished, mobile-friendly browser game called **Orbital Pop Command**, a single-screen arcade bubble shooter presented as a cheerful sci-fi mission. The player controls a cute rocket-like launcher fixed at the bottom center of the screen, aims by moving the mouse or dragging a finger, and taps or clicks to fire exactly one colored orb at a time into a hanging staggered grid of glossy bubbles near the top of the playfield.

Build the core loop around five bright bubble colors and classic bubble-shooter rules: fired shots travel quickly, bounce off the left and right walls, and snap into the nearest valid slot in the staggered grid when they hit the ceiling or another bubble. After snapping, flood-fill all connected bubbles of the same color; if the connected group is size 3 or larger, pop the whole cluster, award score, and spawn juicy particle effects. Then detect all active bubbles still connected to the top row and make any unsupported floating bubbles fall or disappear for bonus points. Keep the loop readable and satisfying: aim, bank a shot, create a match, trigger a cascade, score points, repeat.

Use an endless score-attack progression rather than level-based content. Start each run with only the top several rows populated, show the next bubble loaded into the launcher, and end the game when the bubble mass reaches a visible red warning line near the lower part of the screen. Include a start overlay, a game-over overlay with final score and retry button, and a compact in-game HUD showing the current mission score.

The tone should feel bright, accessible, and arcade-satisfying rather than aggressive. Present the game as a space command mission with a dark starfield background, subtle floating geometric parallax, glassy sci-fi interface panels, glowing text, and a polished rocket launcher with personality. Add looping background music plus distinct sound effects for firing, snapping into place, popping clusters, triggering combos, pressing UI buttons, and failing. For big clears or cascades, briefly show a celebratory animated reaction overlay; on defeat, show a failure reaction overlay. Preserve simple controls, quick restart flow, and strong visual clarity on both desktop and mobile.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## High-level code structure
- Single-file browser game implemented entirely in `index.html`.
- Structure is divided into:
  - HTML UI shell: start screen, HUD, game-over screen, GIF feedback overlay, and full-screen canvas.
  - Embedded CSS: space-themed HUD styling, responsive layout rules, and presentation polish.
  - Embedded JavaScript: asset configuration, audio/GIF controllers, game state, grid logic, render/update loops, input handling, and UI event wiring.
- No module system or external gameplay scripts are used; all systems live inside a `DOMContentLoaded` callback.

## Game loop / state model
- The game uses a lightweight real-time loop split into two functions:
  - `update()`: advances projectile motion, particle effects, collision checks, snapping, cluster resolution, floating-cluster cleanup, and background parallax state.
  - `draw()`: continuously renders the background, active grid bubbles, projectile, particles, launcher rocket, next-bubble preview, and danger line.
- `requestAnimationFrame(draw)` runs continuously so the animated backdrop remains alive even when a match is not in progress.
- `requestAnimationFrame(update)` is only chained while `gameActive` is true.
- Core state variables include:
  - `gameActive`
  - `score`
  - `grid`
  - `projectile`
  - `nextBubbleType`
  - `shooterAngle`
  - `particles`
  - `highestClusterChain`
- Session flow:
  1. Start screen shown.
  2. Player taps/clicks start.
  3. Grid initializes with top rows populated.
  4. Active play continues until clusters are cleared or the stack reaches the danger threshold.
  5. Game-over overlay appears with final score and retry button.

## Player goals
- Aim the launcher from the bottom of the screen.
- Fire colored bubbles into the hanging field.
- Create groups of 3 or more matching bubbles to clear them.
- Cause unsupported bubbles to detach for bonus score.
- Prevent the bubble mass from extending to the lower danger line / bottom loss threshold.

## Interaction pattern
- Mouse move or touch move controls aim direction.
- Click or touch start on the canvas fires one bubble if no projectile is currently active.
- One-shot-at-a-time cadence: the player cannot fire again until the current projectile snaps into the grid.
- Start and restart are explicit button interactions outside the main playfield.
- The control style is arcade-simple and readable on both desktop and mobile.

## Core systems
### 1. Hex-style staggered bubble grid
- Bubble positions are arranged in alternating-offset rows.
- Neighbor lookup changes depending on whether the row is odd or even.
- Grid coordinate conversion maps projectile landing points back into row/column slots.

### 2. Projectile firing and wall bounce
- The launcher sits near the bottom center.
- The projectile inherits the current aim angle.
- Shots bounce off left and right walls before snapping.

### 3. Match detection
- After a projectile snaps, the game performs a flood-fill / breadth-first search to find connected bubbles of the same type.
- Clusters of 3 or more are removed and scored.

### 4. Floating-cluster detection
- A second flood-fill starts from the top row to determine which bubbles remain anchored.
- Any active bubble not connected to the ceiling is considered floating and is removed for bonus points.

### 5. Score and feedback
- Match clears award points based on cluster size.
- Detached floating bubbles give extra bonus points.
- Larger clears trigger combo sound and celebratory GIF feedback.
- Failure triggers a distinct fail sound and fail reaction overlay.

### 6. Audio and juice
- Background music loops during play.
- Separate sound effects are used for shooting, snapping, popping, combos, UI start/restart, and failure.
- Particle bursts and animated overlays reinforce successful clears and defeat.

### 7. Presentation and theming
- The visual wrapper reframes the game as a space-mission bubble popper.
- The launcher is drawn as a stylized rocket/beacon ship.
- Bubbles are rendered as glossy “orb” projectiles.
- HUD language uses mission terminology like “Mission Score,” “Sector Overrun,” and “Launch Mission.”

## Inferred genre / gameplay shape
- Strongest reading: an arcade bubble shooter / match-3 projectile puzzler.
- Secondary qualities:
  - light score attack structure
  - casual mobile-friendly action puzzle
  - single-screen survival pressure due to the loss line
- The game is not level-based in this implementation; it behaves more like an endless score run until the board descends too far.

## Gameplay heuristic
- The intended play loop is:
  1. Read the current projectile and aim line mentally.
  2. Bank or direct a shot into a same-color cluster.
  3. Clear groups efficiently to create larger cascades.
  4. Prefer shots that also disconnect unsupported bubbles.
  5. Keep the field compact and away from the danger threshold.
- Skill comes from angle planning, bounce usage, color matching, and board management rather than reflex-heavy timing.
- Emotional target: bright, approachable, satisfying arcade tension with mild space-hero flavor rather than intense combat.

## Confidence notes
- High confidence that the base mechanic is a bubble-shooter game.
- Medium confidence on progression shape: the present code only shows endless survival/score play, not authored levels.
- High confidence that the space-command fiction is cosmetic framing layered over classic bubble-matching gameplay.
